entities.summary: Oswald of Sussex was an Ealdorman of Sussex, jointly with three former kings: Osmund, Ælfwald, and Oslac, who ruled Sussex from 786 to 796 CE. During his tenure, Oswald oversaw the construction of the Church of St. Peter in Canterbury, which became a major pilgrimage site. He also played a key role in the political instability of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, particularly in the struggle for control of the Kingdom of Northumbria. Oswald's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Church of England and the preservation of Anglo-Saxon cultural heritage. The Oswald of Sussex is remembered as a strong leader who navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the Anglo-Saxon world. His impact on the history of Sussex and the broader Anglo-Saxon world is still felt today, with the Church of St. Peter remaining a significant cultural and historical landmark in the region.
